subtopic: Talking with parents about marriage pressure
passage:
Anirban: Mummy, please tell Bua to stop calling me every night about matches.

Mother: She is only trying to help.

Anirban: I'm not getting married! Never! Do you hear me? Never!

Vijay: Do not raise your voice in this house.

Anirban: Then stop pushing me! It is my life, and I'll never marry, do what you want!

Mother: Anirban, what are you saying?

Vijay: That is enough. Go to your room.

Mother: Now who will keep him calm? He has just said something he won't take back.

Vijay: We will talk to the relatives properly and set the date ourselves.

Anirban: You aren't even listening!

The door slammed. Vijay, the father, stared at the newspaper while Mother sat down in the kitchen and started to cry quietly.

qa.q: Who did Anirban ask Mummy to stop from calling every night?
qa.a: Anirban asked Mummy to stop Bua from calling every night about matches.

qa.q: What was Anirban feeling when shouting the ultimatum?
qa.a: Anirban felt frustrated and cornered after repeated calls from relatives, and shouted to be heard.

qa.q: What could Anirban try instead of the ultimatum, and why?
qa.a: Anirban could wait until calm and say which part of the pressure hurts, because parents may listen once the shouting has stopped.

qa.q: How might Anirban's parents see the outburst?
qa.a: The parents likely felt frightened and anxious, and dug in, since the shout sounded like a rejection of the family.

grounding: A frustrated young adult shouts that they will never marry, and the parents grow more anxious and dig in, ending the conversation.

subtopic: Talking with parents about marriage pressure
passage:
I'm Seema, and last month I did the thing I'd promised myself I would never do.
It was the fourth call that week. First my mother's cousin, then my father's aunt, then a neighbour who'd heard about 'a good boy in Indore'. Then my mother herself, on speaker, while I was in the hostel corridor with my cousin Shreya.
Something snapped. I shouted, 'I am never getting married! Never! Stop calling me!' The whole corridor went silent. On the phone, my mother started crying and handed it to my father, who said very quietly, 'We only wanted to help.' Then he hung up.
Shreya put her hand on my arm. I was shaking.
Since then, my mother has been calling more, not less. Shreya says she's told the aunties to 'find someone quickly before Seema gets more stubborn'. My shouting didn't end anything. It made them more scared, and me more alone.

qa.q: What did Seema shout on the phone?
qa.a: 'I am never getting married! Never! Stop calling me!'

qa.q: How did Seema feel just after shouting, and later?
qa.a: Seema felt shaken and upset, and later lonely, seeing that the outburst had made things worse.

qa.q: What could Seema do now to repair things?
qa.a: Call when calm, apologise for shouting, and share a clearer plan, like finishing studies first, instead of 'never'.

qa.q: How did the outburst look to Seema's parents?
qa.a: They felt hurt and more anxious, which made them push harder to find someone quickly.

grounding: Shows a young adult, worn down by relatives' calls, shouting 'never', which leaves parents more anxious and determined and ends any real talk.

subtopic: Talking with parents about marriage pressure
passage:
Hostel warden's note – Dolma, Boys' Block
At 9:40 last night I heard shouting from the ground-floor phone corner. Ojas, a second-year, was on a call with his parents. I heard him say, 'I will never marry anyone you choose. If you bring one more photo, I'm not coming home at all.' Then he threw the phone onto the bench.
I sat with him afterwards. He said relatives had called six times this week about a match. He is tired, and he is angry. That is understandable.
This morning his mother called me, crying. She said his father has now told the other family they will 'go ahead anyway, he'll come round'. The ultimatum has made them more anxious and more determined, not less.
I've suggested Ojas speak to the college counsellor this week, and think about a calmer call once he has rested. I will check on him on Friday.

qa.q: How many times had relatives called that week?
What was Ojas feeling when he threw the phone onto the bench?
qa.a: He was angry and exhausted, worn down by the calls and pushed into an ultimatum.

qa.q: What could Ojas try in a calmer call?
qa.a: Apologise for the ultimatum, name one thing he needs, like time to finish studying, and ask what worries his parents.

qa.q: How has the outburst affected Ojas's parents?
qa.a: His mother is crying and his father has become more determined, so the ultimatum made them more anxious rather than less.

grounding: Shows a young adult, frustrated by relatives' calls, issuing an angry ultimatum, which leaves parents more anxious and determined and ends the conversation.
